title: Hosted Endpoint PRD: Deployment Cutover, Acceptance Criteria, and Go/No-Go Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket contains the canonical PRD and cutover runbook for a minimal-viable hosted endpoint surface covering chat/completions/embeddings/rerank. Purpose: finalize acceptance criteria, coordinate engineering and design scope changes, and provide an executable go/no-go checklist for the release to hosted-api-2025.11. Scope includes behavioral contracts for API responses, backward compatibility guarantees for existing SDKs, telemetry/alerting targets, release gating, and customer-facing docs updates. Out of scope: large UX redesigns of the Console and non-critical SDK language bindings (to be tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: API contract stability: existing stable endpoints maintain response shape for 99.9% of requests; documented breaking changes behind a feature flag and migration guide
Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 700ms for the minimal config under internal staging workload profile
Cost signal validation: per-token cost estimation matches runtime telemetry within +/- 12% for canary traffic
Quality guardrails: rerank and embeddings produce parity with baseline evals (embedding cosine delta < 0.015 on reference set; rerank NDCG drop < 1.5%)
Rollout controls: canary, staged percentage increases, and automatic rollback on error-rate or latency threshold breach are implemented and tested
Telemetry and alerts: dashboards for per-route latency/cost/error, token-level cost breakdown, and synthetic acceptance tests in Datadog/Chronicle exist and have links
Security/compliance: KMS-authenticated model keys available for Dedicated/Private lanes and security review completed (see links)
Docs and SDKs: public API docs updated, one example integration for chat and embeddings added to repo, and changelog entry prepared
launch_checklist: Pre-cutover sanity run: run smoke suite (end-to-end chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) against staging with production-like traffic profile
Canary deploy: route 1% of traffic to new runtime variant for 4 hours, monitor p95/p99, error rate, and cost metrics
Data plane fallback: validate fallback routing to compatibility model variant under induced capacity constraint
Rollback plan: confirm automated rollback triggers and execute a dry-run rollback in staging
Telemetry validation: ensure synthetic checks pass and dashboards show expected signals within 15 minutes of deployment
SDK compatibility: run language SDK smoke tests (python/node/go) and confirm no client-breaking changes
Security gate: verify KMS integration test and sign-off from Security team
Customer comms: prepare release note, migration guide for any flagged behavioral differences, and support playbook
Post-cutover monitoring: 72h heightened observability with daily review and P0 response path identified
